title: fix(objectql): the boot hydration ERROR names the storage remedies when no driver serves sys_metadata
body:
Fixes #23636

Clause-②: no

## What this changes

When `sys_metadata` cannot be read at boot, `ObjectQLPlugin.restoreMetadataFromDb` logs one `error` line: what was not restored, and the fix. The fix half was always "check the datasource behind sys_metadata — connection, credentials, and that the table exists". On a deployment with no datasource declared and no driver registered, such as a production `os serve` with no `OS_DATABASE_URL`, there is no datasource to check and no credential to fix. The operator was sent to a store nobody configured, with the real remedies absent from the line (they sit on the CLI's `⚠ No storage:` line only, which prints earlier).

Now the line says which situation it is in. When nothing serves `sys_metadata` it says "no storage is configured" and names the three storage remedies, worded exactly as the CLI's `⚠ No storage:` line names them. When a datasource exists and its read failed, the line is byte for byte what it was. Level (`error`) and the consequence sentence are the same in both arms.

## Before / after (the logged text)

Before, in every case:

```text
sys_metadata could NOT be read at boot — persisted metadata was NOT restored, and this kernel will keep reporting healthy. Every overlay object, view, app, permission and hook stored in the database is absent from the SchemaRegistry for the life of this process: registry lookups answer "not declared" rather than "unavailable", so unknown-column query guards, hooks and relationships silently degrade, and overlay objects get neither a synced table nor a metadata bridge. Authoring against this kernel writes on top of state it never loaded. Fix: check the datasource behind sys_metadata — connection, credentials, and that the table exists — then restart. A store that merely has not been provisioned yet is NOT this case; that first-boot path stays quiet.
```

After, when no datasource is declared and no driver serves `sys_metadata`:

```text
sys_metadata could NOT be read at boot — no storage is configured: no datasource is declared and no driver is registered, so nothing serves sys_metadata. Persisted metadata was NOT restored, and this kernel will keep reporting healthy. Every overlay object, view, app, permission and hook stored in the database is absent from the SchemaRegistry for the life of this process: [same consequence sentence as above]. Fix: set OS_DATABASE_URL (e.g. file:./data/app.db, or a postgres:// or mysql:// URL); mount a storage driver in the stack's plugins (e.g. new DriverPlugin(driver) from @objectstack/runtime); or run with --dev (an in-memory SQLite store, for development) — then restart. A store that merely has not been provisioned yet is NOT this case; that first-boot path stays quiet.
```

After, when a datasource exists and its read failed: unchanged from "Before".

## How the arm is chosen

New private `sysMetadataHasNoStorage()`, asked only once the read has already failed (a healthy boot pays nothing). It reads the engine's own routing, never the text of the error the read raised. It answers "no storage" only when all three are empty:

- `getDriverForObject('sys_metadata')`: a driver serves it, so the read itself failed: datasource problem.
- `resolveEffectiveDatasource('sys_metadata')`: it is bound (explicit, mapping, lifecycle or package) to a named datasource whose driver is missing: that datasource is declared, datasource problem.
- `listUnavailableDatasources()`: the connection layer recorded a declared datasource it could not use (policy-refused, or a connect failure the operator waved through): datasource problem. This one matters because such a boot also has no registered driver, so drivers alone cannot tell it from "no storage".

The three remedies live in one `private static readonly NO_STORAGE_REMEDIES` beside the method, with a note that the CLI line is their authority.

File surface: `restoreMetadataFromDb` region of `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, the pins, one changeset. Nothing in `packages/cli`, the start-order region, `onMetadataMutation` or `followRuntimeObjectCopy`.

## Pins and ablation

New `packages/objectql/src/plugin-restore-metadata-no-storage.test.ts` (6 cases), over a real `ObjectQL` engine in every case:

- (a) no storage: the line says "no storage is configured", names the three remedies verbatim, does not contain "check the datasource behind sys_metadata" or "credentials", keeps the consequence sentence, the counts in the meta slot and the single `error`.
- (a, reach) the REAL `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` over a driverless engine: the boot read really fails (`DB hydration skipped: … No driver available for object 'sys_metadata'`) and the line is the no-storage one.
- (b) CONTROL, the datasource arm unchanged, byte for byte: a registered driver whose read fails; the same with the real protocol and a driver that refuses with an authentication error; `sys_metadata` bound to a named datasource with no driver; a declared datasource marked unavailable by the connection layer.

The existing `plugin-restore-metadata-outage.test.ts` used `ql: {}` as its engine on the premise "the engine is untouched by this path". That premise no longer holds, so its `makePlugin()` now builds a real engine with one registered driver (the "a datasource exists and its read failed" shape those cases always meant). Its nine assertions are unchanged.

Ablation, direction predicted before running and observed (mutation applied with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor hit once, blob changed, restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty; the subject is `src/plugin.ts` imported directly, so no rebuild applies):

| mutation | (a) pins | (b) controls | existing outage pins |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| verdict always `false` (branch condition ablated) | 2 RED | 4 green | 9 green |
| verdict always `true` | 2 green | 4 RED | 9 green |
| drop the `getDriverForObject` probe | green | 2 RED (both registered-driver controls) | not run |
| drop the `resolveEffectiveDatasource` probe | green | 1 RED (named binding) | not run |
| drop the `listUnavailableDatasources` probe | green | 1 RED (unavailable datasource) | not run |

So each probe is held by its own control, and no (a) pin passes by accident.

## Verification (every reading at head f273dab8e3)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/plugin-restore-metadata-no-storage.test.ts src/plugin-restore-metadata-outage.test.ts`: 15 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test`: 424 files, 8129 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` (after the last test edit): exit 0; `tsc --noEmit` clean and `check:test-typecheck` OK with the ledger unchanged (39 files, 233 errors held). The new test file is in `tsconfig.test.json`'s program (1 hit) and not in `tsconfig.json`'s (0), which is the layer that compiles tests.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the three changed source and test files: exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 64 commands, plus the 53 artifact-roster and 11 wide-population families it prints; 127 distinct commands, all run: 123 exit 0. Two exit-3 prerequisites (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:published-readme-exports`) were rerun after a full `pnpm build` and are exit 0; `check:type-check-debt` hit my 280 s runner window on the first pass and is exit 0 on its rerun. `dispatch-gates --ran` reconciles 64 derived, 64 run, 0 unrun.
- `check-partof-closing-keyword` needs a pull request body to judge, so it first answered exit 2 (not wired) and was rerun with this body as `PR_BODY`: exit 0.
- NOT MEASURED, each for its reason: `check-closing-target-claim` and `check-single-claim-paths` (exit 2: they read the pull request and the card through the API, and a local run has no pull request yet; CI supplies it) and `pm/check-governed-queue-guard` (exit 1: it reads a workflow event payload; this diff touches no governed surface).

## Acceptance notes

- The three remedies are now spelled in two places: the CLI's `⚠ No storage:` line and `NO_STORAGE_REMEDIES` here. Nothing pins them equal, and sharing one constant would cross into `packages/cli`, outside this card's surface. Noted, not filed (drift not yet exercised).
- The remedies name CLI inputs (`OS_DATABASE_URL`, `--dev`). A host that boots a kernel by hand with no driver reads the same three; "mount a storage driver" is the one that applies to it.
- The line is worded as of the failed read, as it always was. A plugin that registers a driver in its `start()` later does not rewrite what this process already restored.
